metadata.description: Country-level sanctions regimes. additionalWarSanctionsPct is the incremental annual GDP contraction from war-escalation sanctions on top of any existing regime.
sources: IMF World Economic Outlook (2023) — Russia sanctions impact
Neuenkirch & Neumeier (2015), 'The impact of UN and US economic sanctions on GDP growth' — Journal of Development Economics
Hufbauer et al. (2007), 'Economic Sanctions Reconsidered', PIIE Press
Dreyer & Popescu (2014), 'Do economic sanctions work?', Egmont Policy Brief
World Bank (2023) — Iran GDP contraction under JCPOA vs non-JCPOA sanctions
metadata.note: Only countries with well-documented comprehensive or sectoral sanctions are listed. For unlisted aggressors, the sanctions module applies 0 (too speculative without geopolitical context).

RUS.note: IMF estimated 2022 Russia GDP fell ~2.1% vs a +3% baseline = ~5% net impact; 2023 partial recovery. Additional war sanctions (e.g., new conflict) would likely add ~2.5%/yr via tightened energy/finance restrictions.

IRN.regime: US OFAC, UN Security Council, EU comprehensive sanctions (1979–present; tightened 2012, 2018 JCPOA withdrawal)
IRN.note: World Bank/IMF: Iran real GDP fell 6–10%/yr during 2012–2015 and 2018–2020 peak sanctions. Strait of Hormuz context would add ~3%/yr additional pressure on oil sector.

PRK.regime: UN Security Council, US OFAC, EU, South Korea comprehensive sanctions (2006–present)
PRK.note: One of the most sanctioned economies globally. GDP data is sparse; estimates based on UN Panel of Experts reports. Marginal additional impact from new war is limited (already near maximum isolation).

SYR.regime: US, EU, Arab League comprehensive sanctions (2011–present)
SYR.note: Syria GDP fell >50% 2011–2020 due to combined conflict + sanctions. Additional war escalation would add ~2.5%/yr through tightened energy and banking restrictions.

CUB.regime: US OFAC embargo (1962–present); EU and others do not participate
CUB.note: US embargo limits ~15–20% of potential trade. Neuenkirch & Neumeier (2015): unilateral US sanctions reduce target GDP ~1.5–2.5%/yr. Multilateral escalation in a war scenario would add ~1.5%.

VEN.regime: US OFAC targeted + sectoral oil sanctions (2017–present)
VEN.note: US oil sector sanctions cut export revenue ~$6–11B/yr on Venezuela's ~$80B GDP. IMF: structural + sanctions combined pushed GDP contraction. War escalation would likely add EU/UN sanctions.

BLR.regime: US, EU, UK sanctions (expanded post-2020 election crisis; expanded again 2022 after Russian invasion facilitation)
BLR.note: Sectoral sanctions on finance, energy, transport. Closely intertwined with Russian economy; partial isolation from SWIFT. Additional war sanctions ~2%/yr.

MMR.regime: US OFAC, EU, UK targeted sanctions on military junta (post-coup, Feb 2021)
MMR.note: Targeted arms embargo and financial sanctions on junta leadership. Current impact limited vs comprehensive sanctions. War would likely trigger EU/UN arms embargo escalation and broader sectoral sanctions.
